title: Product Showcase Configurator with Budget Conservation
description: Users manage a virtual product showroom with a fixed display-energy budget of 100 units. Three products — a CesiumMilkTruck, a coffee mug, and a Ferrari — sit on individual rotating pedestals. Users allocate spotlight intensity, pedestal height, and rotation speed across all three products, but every change must conserve the total budget. An undo/redo system tracks all configuration states.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a product showcase configurator. Load CesiumMilkTruck.glb, coffeeMug.glb, and ferrari.glb from their paths. Place each model on a cylindrical pedestal (radius 1, height 0.3) arranged in a row with 6-unit spacing along the X axis. Scale models so each fits within a 2x2x2 bounding box. Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 5, 14) looking at the origin, with OrbitControls. Add ambient light (intensity 0.3) and one SpotLight per product aimed downward at each pedestal. Implement a budget-conservation system: total budget is 100 units shared across three channels per product — spotlight intensity (0-20, default 11 each), pedestal height (0-10, default 1 each), rotation speed (0-10 RPM, default 0 each). The sum of all 9 channel values must always equal 100. When the user adjusts any slider, auto-reduce the last-modified other channel on the same product first, then spill reductions across other products proportionally if needed. Build a left-side HTML panel with 9 range sliders (3 groups of 3) labeled by product and channel, plus a live budget counter showing current total locked at 100. Each slider change is an interaction step. Implement undo/redo buttons that push each full 9-value state onto a history stack (max 50 entries). Undo restores the previous state and updates all sliders and 3D scene; redo re-applies. In the render loop, rotate each pedestal group around Y by its rotation speed value, adjust pedestal geometry height, and set spotlight intensity from current values. Add a subtle grid helper on the ground plane. Use a dark background (0x1a1a2e). Ensure all interactions are smooth with no frame drops. The panel should display step count incremented on every slider change, undo, or redo action.
